title: Decoding Strategies
description: Turn a probability distribution over the vocabulary into actual generated text.
content:
A language model ends each step with a probability distribution over the vocabulary; the **decoding strategy** turns distributions into text.

> Decoding strategies:
> • **Greedy** - always take the most probable token; fast and deterministic, but prone to repetitive, bland output
> • **Beam search** - track the b most probable partial sequences and return the overall best; more fluent for closed tasks like translation, though still generic for open-ended generation
> • **Temperature sampling** - divide the logits by T before softmax; T < 1 sharpens the distribution (more deterministic), T > 1 flattens it (more creative)
> • **Top-k** - sample only from the k most likely tokens
> • **Nucleus (top-p)** - sample from the smallest token set whose cumulative probability exceeds p; the candidate set adapts to the shape of the distribution

Supporting processors tune behavior further: **repetition penalties** discourage loops, bad-words lists ban tokens, and length limits with **stopping criteria** (stop at the EOS token) shape the output. In practice, closed structured tasks favor beam search, while open-ended creative text favors nucleus sampling with a tuned temperature.
